record.file_problem: None; the full article text is present. Some benchmark results are shown only as images.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, removes it with activation projection and weight orthogonalization, and reports behavior on a new model.
record.gate_note: The article describes claims from Arditi et al. but those cited findings are not this study's results. Direction scores used to select a candidate and the four generated completions are not reported numerically. Comments appended to the page are not treated as the article's own study results.
record.test_reason: The study computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction on a new model (Daredevil-8B, a Llama-3-8B merge). It removes the direction by weight orthogonalization and reports refusal removal and benchmark changes, so its own results bear on V1 and V2. The evidence is weak: refusal is judged qualitatively on 4 prompts, and those same prompts were used to select the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes that abliteration (weight orthogonalization against the refusal direction) uncensored Daredevil-8B but degraded benchmark performance. DPO healing recovered most of the drop, though not on GSM8K. The resulting NeuralDaredevil-8B is described as fully uncensored and high-quality. The author also says the technique shows how fragile safety fine-tuning is.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless activation mean difference and projection-based ablation, selecting a candidate using four harmful prompts; also performs a weight orthogonalization edit. The article adapts and simplifies an implementation based on FailSpy's notebook and the original authors' notebook.
record.method_sensitivity: The candidate direction is selected by manually checking generations for four harmful prompts; candidate 9 is chosen. The article says other residual streams, instructions, or blocks could be tried if no candidate works. The demonstrated data collection uses English instructions and the last token position.
record.problems: Only four harmful test instructions are used for qualitative refusal evaluation. There is no quantitative refusal rate or uncertainty estimate. Benchmark values are presented in images and not stated in the text; the reported capability decline cannot be quantified from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows extracted. Individual benchmark metrics are visible only in the images, so the reported suite-level declines are recorded as figure-only aggregate results.

Quantitative refusal rate. More than one model. Held-out harmful prompts.

missing.what: Only some of the top-20 candidate directions removed refusal on all 4 prompts; candidate 9 succeeded. This shows sensitivity to layer choice, but the count of failures is not stated.

record.verdict_notes: This is a community blog tutorial, not peer-reviewed. The evidence is thin: 4 prompts, manual selection on the same prompts, a string blacklist screen, and benchmark numbers only in images. Page comments (failures on Llama-3.2-3B, claims of cross-language generalization, Heretic geometry tables) are not the article's results and are excluded. Tranche could arguably be T3 (a new model setting), since the refusal measure is qualitative rather than the original refusal and safety scores.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests was not tested. General capability was evaluated only after weight orthogonalization, not for the inference-time projection intervention.

relation.reason: The author's own runs report refusal removal after ablation and the weight edit, plus benchmark changes, on a model the original did not test. The evidence is weak: 4 in-sample prompts and no rates.

tranche.reason: Same method as Arditi et al. (harmful-minus-harmless mean difference at the last token, projection ablation, weight orthogonalization), adapted from the original authors' notebook via FailSpy. The measure is a weaker form of the original's: a substring filter plus reading 4 completions, and benchmarks. Since the model is new (Daredevil-8B), T3 is arguable, but T1 is defensible.

source_check.notes: The pack listed no [lN] ids, so l1-l4 follow the order of the pack's verdict list. The comments under the article are not the study's results: users say the notebook failed on Llama 3.2 3B, and the author's claim that it 'generalizes very well to other languages' comes with no data. The direction was computed on 256 train-split prompts per set; the 4 test-split prompts were used only to pick the candidate and to check it. Candidates were sorted by abs(mean) of the normalized vector, over resid_pre only, which is not Arditi's selection method.

statements.correction: Labonne: W_E, attention W_O and MLP W_out orthogonalized against candidate 9 (from the top 20 resid_pre candidates, sorted by abs mean). The 4 test-split prompts were used to pick the candidate (human reading plus an 'I cannot'/'I can't' filter). Greedy decoding, 64 tokens. The weight-edited model was pushed as Daredevil-8B-abliterated. No refusal rate and no completions are shown.
statements.problem: Accurate for this study, with one nuance. The text ties 'four instructions' to the inference-time candidate-9 hook. For the weight-orthogonalized model it says only 'successfully uncensored' and tells the reader to verify by printing. The orcarouter numbers are not part of this study and were not checked here.

statements.correction: The post popularized and explained the term ('we introduced the concept of abliteration'), building on FailSpy, whose abliterator library and abliterated-v3 models it cites. No refusal rate. The 4 test prompts were used to select candidate 9. Performance dropped across all benchmarks on the Open LLM Leaderboard and the Nous suite (one image). DPO recovered most of the drop except GSM8K.
statements.problem: 'The post that coined the term' is not supported by the text. The post introduces 'a technique called "abliteration"' and cites FailSpy's earlier abliterator library and his abliterated models. The rest is correct: no refusal rate, 4 prompts used for selection, drops across all benchmarks, DPO healing.
